findings.quote: To find the GCF with prime powers, factor each number. Keep only prime factors shared by every number, then use the smallest exponent for each shared prime.

lesson-arithmetic-number-sense-prime-fac.quote: A common continuous-division mistake is to divide only by primes common to every row. That method can fail for $3$ or more numbers if you then multiply the remaining bottom row.

lesson-arithmetic-number-sense-prime-fac.quote: For a same-remainder problem, subtract the common remainder first. The remainder must be less than every divisor. The remaining part must be divisible by each divisor, so an LCM can describe the repeating values.

lesson-arithmetic-number-sense-prime-fac.quote: A **composite number** is an integer greater than $1$ with more than two positive factors. For example, $12$ is composite because it has factors besides $1$ and $12$.
